cases.name: a portable widget is accepted
cases.why: The ordinary case: bindings plus instruments core knows. Every client draws this, hc-tui included, and no core release was needed to add it.

cases.name: code registered against a render is accepted
cases.why: The Lovelace case. hc-web draws the sandboxed document; every other client draws the gauge. The code is an attachment to the portable description, not a replacement for it.

cases.name: code without a render is rejected
cases.why: THE portability guarantee. A widget that only a browser can draw would make hc-web the only viable homeCore UI, which is exactly what the two-class split exists to prevent — so it is refused where the declaration arrives, not where it fails to draw.
cases.error: widget 'boiler_flow' declares code but no render: a code widget must still say what a client without a browser draws

cases.name: no render at all is rejected
cases.why: A widget nothing can draw. Read differently from the case above, because a plugin that has not started is not making the same mistake as one that shipped code and stopped.

cases.name: an unknown element kind is rejected
cases.why: The opposite of an unknown widget `type`, which core accepts on purpose. A type core has never seen is a card some client may still draw; an element kind no client knows is a hole in the page.
cases.error: widget 'boiler_flow' renders unknown element 'sparkline' (expected column, gauge, icon, row, shape, stack, text)

cases.name: an unknown field on a known element is rejected
cases.why: Strict, where a widget config is not. An unknown config key is a client's own drawing preference riding along; an unknown render field is a plugin asking every client to draw something none of them agreed to.

cases.name: a half-specified range is rejected
cases.why: All four bounds or none. A mapping missing one bound is the case where a gauge quietly reads 0-1 — a card that looks like it works until somebody checks it against the boiler.
cases.error: widget 'boiler_flow' binding 'flow' gives 3 of in_from, in_to, out_from, out_to (all four or none)

cases.name: a complete range is accepted
cases.why: The same binding with the fourth bound. Lifted out of hc-web's SvgBinding so a mapping means one thing whether it feeds a portable gauge or a sandboxed drawing.

cases.name: a missing required field is rejected
cases.why: A gauge with nothing to show is not a gauge.

cases.name: a value outside one_of is rejected, and the message says what would work
cases.why: Arriving here is nearly always a typo, so the error names the offending value and the legal ones.
cases.error: widget 'boiler_flow' element 'gauge' field 'shape' has unsupported value 'dial' (expected radial, bar)

cases.name: a container holds children
cases.why: row, column and stack are the only kinds that may. Everything else draws itself.

cases.name: children on an instrument are rejected
cases.why: A text with children is a mistake worth naming rather than ignoring — ignoring it means one client draws them and the rest do not.
cases.error: widget 'boiler_flow' gives children to 'text', which draws itself

cases.name: a bad field inside a child is rejected
cases.why: The tree is validated all the way down. A render that is legal at the root and broken two levels in is the shape that would otherwise reach a client.

cases.name: a negative thickness is rejected
cases.why: Geometry has bounds, and `number` is spelled in this table and nowhere in the widget-config vocabulary, which has no float field.
cases.error: widget 'boiler_flow' element 'gauge' field 'thickness' must be at least 0

cases.name: a widget with no title is rejected
cases.why: The title is human-facing and owned by the plugin. Core's own widgets have none here because every client already has labels for those; a plugin card has nowhere else to get one.
